                Rebuttal Testimony of Justin Bieber in Support of Stipulation

 1                                  I. INTRODUCTION

 2   Q.   PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME AND BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 3   A.   My name is Justin Bieber. My business address is 111 E Broadway, Suite 1200,

 4        Salt Lake City, Utah, 84111.

 5   Q.   ARE YOU THE SAME JUSTIN BIEBER WHO PREVIOUSLY FILED

 6        DIRECT TESTIMONY AND STIPULATION TESTIMONY IN THIS

 7        PROCEEDING ON BEHALF OF                      THE NEW MEXICO LARGE

 8        CUSTOMER GROUP (“NMLCG”)?

 9   A.   Yes, I am.

10   Q.   WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR REBUTTAL TESTIMONY IN

11        SUPPORT OF THE STIPULATION?

12   A.   My rebuttal testimony in support of the Comprehensive Stipulation (“Stipulation”)

13        responds to the testimony in opposition of the Stipulation of the New Mexico Public

14        Regulation Commission (“NMPRC” or “Commission”) Utility Division Staff

15        (“Staff”) witnesses Daren K. Zigich and Ed Rilkoff. Specifically, I address Mr.

16        Zigich’s opposition to Condition 1.11 of the Comprehensive Stipulation and Mr.

17        Rilkoff's opposition to the stipulated class revenue allocation. As discussed further

18        below, it is my position that Staff’s testimony does not provide persuasive evidence




                                                1
                                          Case No. 25-00079-UT
                        Rebuttal Testimony of Justin Bieber in Support of Stipulation

 1              to reject the Stipulation and I believe that the Commission should approve the

 2              Stipulation in whole.

 3   II. RESPONSE TO MR. ZIGICH’S TESTIMONY REGARDING 1 CP SYSTEM

 4                                   LOAD FACTOR CALCULATIONS

 5   Q.         PLEASE SUMMARIZE CONDITION 1.11 OF THE STIPULATION.

 6   A.         Condition 1.11 of the Stipulation documents the Signatories’ agreement regarding

 7              four issues in this case:

 8              1.       Southwestern Public Service Company (“SPS” or the “Company”) shall

 9                       allocate all costs of production and transmission, including Hale and

10                       Sagamore wind generation, on an average-and-excess demand four-

11                       coincident peak (“AED-4CP”) basis;

12              2.       SPS shall allocate Production Tax Credits (“PTCs”) on an energy basis;

13              3.       The system load factor used in the AED 4-CP calculations will be calculated

14                       using the system single peak demand for the year (“1 CP”); and

15              4.       Documents the Signatories agreement on the stipulated base rate revenue

16                       allocation shown in Exhibit A of the Stipulation.1




     1
         Comprehensive Stipulation, pp. 9-10 (Jun. 22, 2026).

                                       Case No. 25-00079-UT
                     Rebuttal Testimony of Justin Bieber in Support of Stipulation

 1   Q.      WHAT IS MR. ZIGICH’S CONCERN REGARDING SECTION 1.11?

 2   A.      Mr. Zigich asserts the system 1 CP demand term in Condition 1.11 of the

 3           Stipulation conflicts with the Case No. 25-00085-UT stipulation, in particular

 4           Section I.1.3, Condition C.2 According to Mr. Zigich, the Case No. 25-00085-UT

 5           stipulation was based on an agreement by SPS to review and modify its cost

 6           allocation methodology to better align with a growing renewable energy and energy

 7           storage portfolio.3 This review, according to Mr. Zigich, should assess customer

 8           class impacts on the SPS system over more hours than the four peaks considered in

 9           the existing AED-4CP method.4

10                    Mr. Zigich contrasts that objective with Condition 1.11 of the Stipulation in

11           this proceeding, which he characterizes as reducing the number of peak hours from

12           four to one, as highlighted by Occidental Permian, Ltd. (“OPL”) witness Jonathan

13           Ly in his testimony in support of the Stipulation.5 Based on this comparison, Mr.

14           Zigich recommends that the Commission should not approve Condition 1.11 of the

     5

 1              Stipulation unless Condition 1.11 is revised to be consistent with Section I.1.3,

 2              Condition C of the Case No. 25-00085-UT stipulation.6

 3   Q.         WHAT IS THE CASE NO. 25-00085-UT STIPULATION LANGUAGE

 4              THAT MR. ZIGICH ASSERTS CONFLICTS WITH THE STIPULATION

 5              IN THIS CASE?

 6   A.         As I explain above, Mr. Zigich contends that the Stipulation is inconsistent with

 7              Section I.1.3 Condition C of the Stipulation in Case 25-00085-UT. Section I.1.3

 8              Condition C of the Stipulation in Case 25-00085-UT states that:

 9                      “SPS shall convene a working group with stakeholders and Staff to
10                      evaluate and analyze alternatives to SPS’s current retail customer
11                      class cost allocation for both demand (capacity) and energy costs.
12                      The results of this analysis will be presented in SPS’s next rate
13                      case.”7

14   Q.         WHAT       IS    YOUR       RESPONSE          TO     MR.      ZIGICH’S      CONCERN

15              REGARDING CONDITION 1.11 OF THE STIPULATION IN THIS

16              PROCEEDING?

17   A.         The provision of the Stipulation in this case—which directs SPS to use the system

18              1 CP to calculate the load factor for purposes of developing the AED-4CP



     6
         Id. at p. 5.
     7
         Case No. 25-00085-UT, Unanimous Comprehensive Stipulation, p. 6 (Apr. 10, 2026).




                                                         4
                                          Case No. 25-00079-UT
                        Rebuttal Testimony of Justin Bieber in Support of Stipulation

 1              allocation factors—is not inconsistent with the Case No. 25-00085-UT stipulation

 2              provision that directs SPS to convene a working group with stakeholders and Staff

 3              to evaluate and analyze alternatives to SPS’s current retail customer class cost

 4              allocation for demand and energy costs.

 5                       Further, it is important to note that Stipulation Condition 1.11 is actually

 6              almost identical to Staff witness Larry Blank’s recommendation in direct

 7              testimony. Specifically, Dr. Blank recommended:

 8                       “For future rate cases, I recommend that the system load factor used
 9                       to weight average demand in the average and excess demand
10                       allocation method be calculated using the single system peak
11                       demand, rather than the four-month average system peak used to
12                       compute the excess demands.”8

13              In fact, the only difference between Staff witness Dr. Blank’s recommendation and

14              Stipulation Condition 1.11 regarding the use of the 1 CP is that Dr. Blank

15              recommends applying the 1 CP calculation in future SPS rate cases. Accordingly,

16              it is difficult to reconcile Mr. Zigich’s criticism of the Stipulation’s use of the

17              system 1 CP with Dr. Blank’s recommendation advocating essentially the same

18              modification to the AED-4CP methodology.




     8
         Direct Testimony of Larry Blank, p. 14, lines 14-19 (May 1, 2026).




                                                           5
                                       Case No. 25-00079-UT
                     Rebuttal Testimony of Justin Bieber in Support of Stipulation

 1   Q.      PLEASE             SUMMARIZE                  YOUR          CONCLUSIONS                 AND

 2           RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING STAFF WITNESS MR. ZIGICH’S

 3           CONCERNS WITH CONDITION 1.11 OF THE STIPULATION.

 4   A.      I do not agree with Mr. Zigich’s assertion that Condition 1.11 of the Stipulation is

 5           inconsistent with the Commission-approved stipulation in Case No. 25-00085-UT.9

 6           The prior Stipulation in Case No. 25-00085-UT commits SPS to work

 7           collaboratively with Staff and stakeholders to evaluate and analyze alternative

 8           customer class cost allocation methodologies in future proceedings and to present

 9           the results of that analysis in SPS’s next rate case.10 Condition 1.11 of the

10           Stipulation in this proceeding addresses the use of the system single coincident peak

11           to calculate the system load factor used in developing the AED-4CP allocation

12           factors in this rate case and does not prevent or undermine that commitment. It is

13           the NMLCG’s understanding that SPS will still convene a working group with

14           stakeholders and Staff to evaluate class cost allocation methodologies to be

15           presented in the next rate case, consistent with the Stipulation in Case No. 25-

16           00085-UT.


     9
      See Daren K. Zigich Testimony in Opposition of Comprehensive Stipulation, p. 4.
     10
        Case No. 25-00085-UT, Certification of Stipulation, Exhibit A (Unanimous Comprehensive Stipulation),
     p. 6, Sec. 1.3(c) (May 19, 2026).




                                                       6
                                      Case No. 25-00079-UT
                    Rebuttal Testimony of Justin Bieber in Support of Stipulation

 1                   Moreover, the specific aspect of Condition 1.11 identified by Mr. Zigich is

 2           consistent with the recommendation previously advanced by Staff witness Dr.

 3           Larry Blank in this proceeding. Specifically, Dr. Blank recommended using the

 4           system 1 CP to calculate the system load factor within the AED-4CP methodology

 5           in future rate cases.11

 6                   Dr. Blank’s testimony in support of using the system 1 CP to calculate the

 7           system load factor is also consistent with my recommendation in my direct

 8           testimony, except that I recommended incorporating the modification in this rate

 9           case, as opposed to waiting to incorporate the modification until SPS’s next rate

10           case. In addition to myself and Dr. Blank, OPL witness Mr. Ly and Walmart

11           witness Dr. McGovern also recommended in direct testimony that the AED load

12           factor calculations should utilize the system 1CP instead of the 4CP.12

13                   Accordingly, Mr. Zigich’s Testimony in Opposition to the Stipulation

14           contradicts positions Staff (and other parties) have taken in this case and has not

15           identified a valid basis for rejecting Condition 1.11. Thus, I recommend that the

16           Commission approve the Stipulation as filed.


     11
      Direct Testimony of Larry Blank, p. 14 (May 1, 2026).
     12
      Direct Testimony of Jonathan Ly, p. 14 (May 1, 2026); Direct Testimony of Dr. Jaime Lyndsey
     McGovern, p. 18 (May 1, 2026).

 1        III. RESPONSE TO MR. RILKOFF’S TESTIMONY REGARDING CLASS

 2                                         REVENUE ALLOCATION

 3   Q.         PLEASE EXPLAIN STAFF WITNESS MR. RILKOFF’S CONCERN

 4              REGARDING THE STIPULATION’S CLASS REVENUE ALLOCATION?

 5   A.         Mr. Rilkoff contends the Stipulation’s class revenue allocation, which increases

 6              residential and small customer classes’ base rates by 17.5%, is too high and not

 7              adequately justified when compared with Staff’s filed evidence. Mr. Rilkoff asserts

 8              that, from an affordability and customer impact perspective, Dr. Blank’s testimony

 9              provides a more reasonable basis for resolving the allocation and rate design issues

10              in this case.13

11   Q.         HOW DOES THE STIPULATION’S CLASS REVENUE ALLOCATION

12              COMPARE            TO      STAFF’S         RECOMMENDED                 CLASS        REVENUE

13              ALLOCATION?

 3        stipulated increase relative to the system average.

 4   Q.   WHAT IS YOUR ASSESSMENT OF STAFF’S RECOMMENDED CLASS

 5        REVENUE ALLOCATION COMPARED TO THE STIPULATION?

 6   A.   Both Staff's recommended class revenue allocation and the stipulated revenue

 7        allocation move customer classes closer to cost of service while also incorporating

 8        the principle of gradualism.      However, when the different overall revenue

 9        requirements are considered, the Stipulation actually provides a greater degree of

10        rate moderation for the Residential and Small General Service classes compared to

11        Staff’s recommendation.

12               For example, as shown in Table JB-1, Staff’s recommended revenue

13        allocation would result in Residential customers receiving a base rate increase equal

14        to 164.5% of the system average, while the Stipulation provides a Residential

15        increase equal to 139.5% of the system average. Similarly, Staff’s recommendation

16        would result in Small General Service customers receiving a base rate increase

17        equal to 183.9% of the system average, whereas the Stipulation provides an

18        increase equal to 139.5% of the system average.




                                               10
                             Case No. 25-00079-UT
           Rebuttal Testimony of Justin Bieber in Support of Stipulation

 1          The principal difference between Staff’s recommendation and the

 2   Stipulation is not how the revenue increase is allocated among customer classes,

 3   but rather the amount of revenue to be collected. The Stipulation reflects an overall

 4   base revenue increase of approximately 12.5%, while Staff recommended an

 5   overall base revenue increase of approximately 6.7%. As a result, all customer

 6   classes, except Secondary General Service, experience larger absolute percentage

 7   rate increases under the Stipulation than under Staff’s recommendation because the

 8   total amount of revenue being recovered is substantially higher.

 9          Because the two proposals are based on different overall revenue

10   requirements, simply comparing the percentage rate increase assigned to a

11   particular customer class can be misleading. Expressing each class’s increase

12   relative to the overall system average normalizes the results by removing the effect

13   of the different revenue requirements, and thus clearly details how each proposal

14   allocates the approved revenue requirement among customer classes.

15          In sum, when viewed on this normalized basis, the Stipulation actually

16   provides greater rate moderation for the Residential and Small General Service

17   classes than Staff’s recommendation.




                                          11
                                  Case No. 25-00079-UT
                Rebuttal Testimony of Justin Bieber in Support of Stipulation

 1   Q.   PLEASE          SUMMARIZE              YOUR          CONCLUSIONS              AND

 2        RECOMMENDATIONS REGARDING STAFF WITNESS MR. RILKOFF’S

 3        CONCERNS          WITH       THE      STIPULATED           CLASS       REVENUE

 4        ALLOCATION.

 5   A.   Mr. Rilkoff’s criticism of the stipulated class revenue allocation does not

 6        appropriately distinguish between the overall jurisdictional revenue requirement

 7        and the allocation of that revenue requirement among customer classes. While I

 8        recognize that Staff has separate concerns regarding the magnitude of the stipulated

 9        revenue requirement, those concerns are distinct from whether the stipulated class

10        revenue allocation reasonably allocates the approved revenue requirement among

11        the customer classes.

12               When the stipulated revenue allocation is compared to Staff’s

13        recommendation on a normalized basis that accounts for the differing overall

14        revenue requirements, the Stipulation actually provides a greater degree of rate

15        moderation for the Residential and Small General Service classes than Staff’s

16        recommended revenue allocation. Accordingly, I do not agree with Mr. Rilkoff’s

17        suggestion that, from a class revenue allocation perspective, the Stipulation treats

18        those customer classes less favorably than Staff’s proposal.




                                              12
                                   Case No. 25-00079-UT
                 Rebuttal Testimony of Justin Bieber in Support of Stipulation

 1                In my opinion, the stipulated class revenue allocation appropriately

 2        balances the objectives of moving customer classes toward cost-based rates while

 3        recognizing the importance of gradualism and mitigating customer rate impacts.

 4        The Stipulation revenue allocation is also supported by several parties that represent

 5        different customer class interests, including the New Mexico Department of Justice

 6        which represents residential and small commercial customers.            Therefore, I

 7        continue to recommend that the Commission approve the stipulated class revenue

 8        allocation.

 9   Q.   DO YOU CONTINUE TO RECOMMEND THAT THE STIPULATED

10        CUSTOMER CLASS REVENUE ALLOCATION IS IN THE PUBLIC

11        INTEREST?

12   A.   Yes. For the reasons explained in my testimony supporting the Stipulation and in

13        this rebuttal testimony, I continue to conclude that the Stipulation represents a

14        reasonable resolution of the issues before the Commission and is in the public

15        interest. Accordingly, I respectfully recommend that the Commission approve the

16        Stipulation in its entirety.

17   Q.   DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

18   A.   Yes, it does.
